title: Cookbook:Ukrainian Cabbage Soup (Kapusniak)
categories: Recipes using chicken broth and stock
ingredients_raw: 2–5 cloves of garlic, peeled and minced
1–2 potatoes, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
4–6 carrots, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
4–5 sticks of celery, sliced into bite-sized pieces
steps: In a large cooking pot heat about 3–4 tablespoons of olive oil. Add the onions and garlic, along with more olive oil if necessary. Let the onions and garlic cook over medium or low heat for 8–10 minutes.
Add the chicken broth, and bring to a boil.

Add the potatoes, carrots, celery, and spices; bring to a boil, and simmer over medium heat until vegetables are almost tender enough to eat. If the soup becomes too thick, add some more chicken broth, but it should be a hearty soup with plenty of vegetables.
Season with salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, seasoning salt, garlic salt, and or celery salt as desired.
Add the can of tomatoes and the shredded cabbage. Again, let the soup simmer over medium heat; continue tasting to see whether your imagination has worked magic.
Lastly, add the chopped fresh dill.
When it’s done, serve garnished with sour cream.
description: Kapustnik is a hearty Central and Eastern European raw cabbage soup. It must be not confused with Kapusniak which is made of sauerkraut.

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Ukraine|Ukrainian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]] 

'''Kapustnik''' is a hearty Central and Eastern European raw [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]] [[Cookbook:Soups|soup]]. It must be not confused with Kapusniak which is made of sauerkraut.

==Ingredients==
===Soup===
*[[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
*2 medium-size [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2–5 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
*1 litre or more [[Cookbook:Chicken Broth|chicken broth]]
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
*4–6 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces
*4–5 sticks of [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]], sliced into bite-sized pieces
*Pickling spices
*[[Cookbook:Sage|Sage]]
*[[Cookbook:Thyme|Thyme]]
*[[Cookbook:Oregano|Oregano]]
*[[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|Bay leaves]], 
*[[Cookbook:Rosemary|Rosemary]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
*[[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire sauce]]
*[[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|Soy sauce]]
*[[Cookbook:Seasoning Salt|Seasoning salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Garlic Salt|Garlic salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Celery Salt|Celery salt]]
*1 large can of diced [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*1 head of [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], sliced
*Fresh [[Cookbook:Dill|dill]], chopped

===Garnish===
*[[Cookbook:Sour Cream|Sour cream]] or [[Cookbook:Yoghurt|yoghurt]]

==Procedure==
# In a large cooking pot heat about 3–4 tablespoons of olive oil. Add the onions and garlic, along with more olive oil if necessary. Let the onions and garlic cook over medium or low heat for 8–10 minutes.
# Add the chicken broth, and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Add the potatoes, carrots, celery, and spices; bring to a boil, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] over medium heat until vegetables are almost tender enough to eat. If the soup becomes too thick, add some more chicken broth, but it should be a hearty soup with plenty of vegetables.
# Season with salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, seasoning salt, garlic salt, and or celery salt as desired.
# Add the can of tomatoes and the shredded cabbage. Again, let the soup simmer over medium heat; continue tasting to see whether your imagination has worked magic.
# Lastly, add the chopped fresh dill.
# When it’s done, serve [[Cookbook:Garnish|garnished]] with sour cream.
